assessment.name: Notice retention review after V2 activation
assessment.description: This synthetic notice service is publicly reachable and operated by an entity offering the service to the public. Review its notice retention.

criteria.rationale: The system configures a 7-day retention period (RETENTION_PERIOD = timedelta(days=7)) but critically miscalculates it. The delete_expired method at line 44 uses 'notice.draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD' to determine expiration, measuring 7 days from the draft timestamp instead of the receipt timestamp as required. This violates the legal requirement that the 7-day period must begin 'from the receipt timestamp' and the qualifier that 'receipt timestamp begins the retention period.' A notice drafted days before receipt would be deleted prematurely.

The database schema defines the notices table with both notice_text (TEXT NOT NULL) and receipt_timestamp (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL) as columns in the same table, ensuring they are stored together. The Notice dataclass in service.py also binds these fields together in a single record structure. Every notice record contains both the text and its receipt timestamp as part of the same stored entity.

The receive method accepts receipt_timestamp as an explicit parameter (line 24) and stores it directly in the Notice record (line 30). This timestamp is passed in by the caller at the point of notice receipt, not derived from the draft_timestamp. The schema and dataclass both maintain receipt_timestamp as a distinct field from draft_timestamp, confirming that the receipt timestamp is recorded when the notice is received, not when drafted.

The Notice dataclass is declared frozen=True (line 9), making all fields immutable after creation. The notice_text field is stored as-is with no transformation logic. The NoticeService class has only three methods (receive, get, delete_expired) verified through code graph analysis - none modify notice text. Comprehensive searches (grep for replace, strip, sanitize, remove, filter, clean, transform, update, set, edit, modify, lower, upper, limiting, truncate) found zero text-processing matches. Direct inspection of all source files confirmed no text modification code exists. The frozen dataclass design and verified absence of any text-processing logic ensures that notice text, including any limiting language, is preserved exactly as received.

decision.rationale: The rule applies because the customer has confirmed that this notice service is offered to the public by its operator, is publicly reachable, and is not private household use. The applicability condition 'Operator offers the notice service to the public (not private household use)' is satisfied. The system stores notice records (notice text with receipt timestamps) and applies retention logic, falling within the rule's scope.
